title: Entity-relationship diagram: mscms\_training database
caption: Entity-relationship diagram of the \texttt{mscms\_training} database, showing the matches subsystem (formations, line-ups, events and per-player statistics), the database-backed competition subsystem (teams and fixtures), and the training subsystem (plans, drills and attendance) with their principal columns and foreign-key relationships.
notes: Verified: standalone wf_er-training.tex compiled with pdflatex, no "! " errors, single A4 page. Faithful to Appendix C.3: 12 principal tables of mscms_training with 3-4 key columns each (PK/FK underlined). Column names trimmed to fit (e.g. home/away_score for home_team_score/away_team_score; stats for the flat sport-specific statistics columns; perf_score for performance_score). The schema lists training_plans and training_drills as one combined row sharing training_session_id; I depict them as separate entities (both FK training_session_id) per the diagram brief. PLAYER_TRAINING_ASSESSMENTS exists only as an API endpoint, not a distinct schema table (post-session assessment data lives in training_attendance.performance_score), so it is represented by TRAINING_ATTENDANCE rather than a separate box. Long relationship paths (COMPETITION->MATCHES "groups" over the top; COMPETITION_TEAM->COMPETITION_FIXTURE "schedules" around the right) are routed with manual orthogonal \draw paths so no connector crosses through an entity box. Whole picture wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} as required.

label: fig-er-medical
title: Entity-relationship diagram: mscms\_medical database
caption: Entity-relationship diagram for the \texttt{mscms\_medical} database, showing the staged injury journey (injuries owning diagnoses, treatments and rehabilitations, with rehabilitations driving recovery programmes) alongside the independent fitness-test and training-load records.
latex:
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=14mm]
  % central injury record and its staged journey
  \Entity{inj}{INJURIES}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    teamId\\
    injuryType\\
    severity\\
    injuredBodyPart\\
    injuryDate\\
    expectedRecoveryDate\\
    status}
  \Entity[right=30mm of inj]{dia}{DIAGNOSES}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    \underline{FK} injuryId\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    diagnosis\\
    testResults\\
    recommendations}
  \Entity[above=12mm of dia]{trt}{TREATMENTS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    \underline{FK} injuryId\\
    treatmentType\\
    status\\
    startDate\\
    endDate}
  \Entity[below=12mm of dia]{reh}{REHABILITATIONS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    \underline{FK} injuryId\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    programmeDetail\\
    status}
  \Entity[right=30mm of reh]{rec}{RECOVERY\_PROGRAMS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    \underline{FK} rehabilitationId\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    programmeDetail}
  % independent fitness / load entities
  \Entity[below=14mm of reh]{fit}{FITNESS\_TESTS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    teamId\\
    testType\\
    sportType\\
    testDate\\
    result\\
    resultCategory}
  \Entity[right=30mm of fit]{tld}{TRAINING\_LOADS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    intensity\\
    load}
  % relationships
  \Rel{inj}{trt}{1}{*}{has}
  \Rel{inj}{dia}{1}{*}{has}
  \Rel{inj}{reh}{1}{*}{has}
  \Rel{reh}{rec}{1}{*}{drives}
\end{tikzpicture}%
}
notes: Compiled cleanly on first attempt (pdflatex exit 0, single page, no "! " errors). Columns taken from Appendix C section C.4. The "programmeDetail" column for rehabilitations/recovery_programs is abstracted because the appendix itself abbreviates those as "programme detail". Per the prompt's intended model, RECOVERY_PROGRAMS FK is shown as rehabilitationId (the appendix literally lists injury_id for that table). Wrapped in \resizebox to fit the A4 text width because the seven-entity layout is wide.

label: fig-er-notification

caption: Entity-relationship diagram of the \texttt{mscms\_notification} database, showing notifications, alerts, and the team-chat groups, members, and threaded messages.
notes: Verified by compiling documentation/_probe/wf_er-notification.tex with pdflatex (clean, 1 page, no "! " errors). Uses only \Entity/\Rel/lbl/dLine from preamble-diagrams.tex, wrapped in \resizebox to text width. Entities/fields match Appendix C section C.5 (06-appendices.tex): the physical columns are recipient_user_keycloak_id, status (mapped to read), message (mapped to body), alert_type/target_user, created_by_keycloak_id (ownerKeycloakId), user_keycloak_id (memberKeycloakId), invited_by_keycloak_id, parent_message_id; field names were rendered as the camelCase entity-level names requested in the brief. NOTIFICATIONS and ALERTS are standalone (no FK relationships in the schema), so they are shown unconnected. The MESSAGES self-reference (parentMessageId threads) is drawn as a curved self-loop labelled "replies to 0..1". Two benign Overfull \hbox warnings only.

label: fig-er-reports
title: Entity-relationship diagram: mscms\_reports database
caption: Entity-relationship diagram of the \texttt{mscms\_reports} database, whose analytical entities aggregate operational data from other domains through opaque cross-service references rather than foreign-key constraints.
latex:
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=8mm]
  \Entity{ma}{MATCH\_ANALYSIS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    matchId\\
    teamId\\
    sportType\\
    sportSpecificStats\\
    tacticalAnalysis\\
    playerRatings}
  \Entity[right=10mm of ma]{pa}{PLAYER\_ANALYTICS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    playerKeycloakId\\
    teamId\\
    sportType\\
    primaryScore\\
    secondaryScore\\
    averageRating}
  \Entity[right=10mm of pa]{ta}{TEAM\_ANALYTICS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    teamId\\
    sportType\\
    wins / draws / losses\\
    pointsFor\\
    pointsAgainst}
  \Entity[below=8mm of ma]{tr}{TRAINING\_ANALYTICS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    teamId\\
    aggregate training\\ \quad metrics}
  \Entity[below=8mm of pa]{sr}{SCOUT\_REPORTS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    scoutKeycloakId\\
    outerPlayerId\\
    ratings\\
    recommendation}
  \Entity[below=8mm of ta]{sc}{SPONSOR\_CONTRACT\_OFFERS}{%
    \underline{PK} id\\
    sponsorKeycloakId\\
    offerTitle\\
    contractValue\\
    sponsorshipType\\
    status}
  \node[lbl, draw=dLine, fill=dFill, text width=46mm, align=center,
        below=11mm of sr] (note)
    {\itshape Entities are independent; cross-domain links
     (matchId, teamId, player\slash scout\slash sponsor Keycloak ids)

\end{tikzpicture}
notes: Faithful to Appendix C section C.5 (06-appendices.tex lines 459-465): six entities with their exact key columns from the schema table, rendered in camelCase to match the domain DTOs. No \Rel connectors are drawn because these tables carry no foreign keys — they aggregate other domains by opaque id; this design fact is captured in an explanatory note box instead. The picture is about 12cm wide and fits the 13.5cm text block, so no resizebox was needed. Verified: pdflatex exit 0, single page, no "! " errors and no overfull hbox warnings. team_analytics wins/draws/losses combined onto one row and training_analytics columns abbreviated as "aggregate training metrics" (the schema itself lists them only as "aggregate training metrics") to keep box heights even.

label: fig-seq-login
title: Sequence diagram: authentication and JWT issuance
caption: Sequence diagram of the authentication flow: credentials submitted on the front-end traverse the gateway and the user-management service, which performs an OAuth~2.0 password-grant exchange at Keycloak to obtain and return the JWT access token and role.
notes: Verified by compiling documentation/_probe/wf_seq-login.tex with pdfLaTeX: exit 0, single page (26791 bytes), no "! " error lines in the log. Five instances exactly (User thread + Frontend, Gateway, user-management, Keycloak), per the <=5 cap. Wrapped in \resizebox to \textwidth since the four nested call/return blocks make the diagram wider than the A4 text block. Message order follows the enumerated "Authentication and Session Establishment" steps in chapters/03-methodology.tex (POST /auth/login, gateway forward, OAuth2 password-grant at Keycloak token endpoint, access+refresh tokens returned, access token+role relayed back, then the front-end self-message decoding the JWT to read sub=keycloakId and realm roles before storing the token and role). Token/grant detail (grant_type=password, realm mscms) abbreviated in labels to keep the boxes compact.

label: fig-seq-schedule
title: Sequence diagram: scheduling an official match with line-up
caption: Sequence diagram for scheduling an official match: the coach builds the formation and starting eleven from a competition fixture, the training-match service validates the kick-off time and line-up, and on success persists the Match, MatchFormation and MatchLineup atomically in a single transaction so a match can never exist without a starting eleven.
notes: Verified with a standalone pdfLaTeX compile (single page, no "! " errors, no overfull boxes). Uses pgf-umlsd with five instances (Coach thread, Frontend, Gateway, training-match, DB) and an sdblock "validate" alt holding both the [invalid] 400 branch and the [ok] atomic-persist branch. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} because the validate-block guard text runs wide; this guarantees it fits the ~13.5cm A4 text block. Service names (training-match service on port 8087, /matches endpoint, createMatch) and entity names (Match, MatchFormation/match_formations, MatchLineup/match_lineups) match Appendix C and the methodology subsection "Scheduling an Official Match from a Competition Fixture". The [invalid] self-message is modelled with a messcall (no return label) since pgf-umlsd's call/sdblock cannot cleanly express a true mutually-exclusive alt; both branches are shown inside one validate frame.

label: fig-seq-live
title: Sequence diagram: live-match phase progression and goal event
caption: Sequence diagram of live-match phase progression and goal recording, showing the broadcast phase machine (first half, half-time, second half, full-time) and the minute-bounding validation that rejects out-of-phase goals before persisting the event and updating the score.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdfLaTeX (exit 0, single A4 page, no "! " errors). Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} so the five-lifeline diagram fits the 13.5cm text block; one benign 17.6pt Overfull hbox during measurement, harmless after scaling. Facts verified against documentation: service is training-match (port 8087, /match-events endpoint), match_events table columns event_type/minute, matches table home_team_score/away_team_score, and the phase order FirstHalf -> HalfTime -> SecondHalf -> FullTime. The alt's reject leg uses a self-call (svc->svc, 422) since a one-sided reject before persistence reads cleanly in pgf-umlsd; the trailing \footnotesize note line is part of the snippet body (outside the sequencediagram) and renders below the picture.

label: fig-seq-injury-sub
title: Sequence diagram: in-match injury and forced substitution
caption: Sequence diagram for an in-match injury and the forced substitution it triggers, showing how training-match persists the INJURY match event while delegating to medical-fitness to create the real injury record before the operator records the substitution.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdfLaTeX via the probe2.tex wrapper: 1 page, no "! " errors, no overfull boxes. Uses only pgf-umlsd (loaded by preamble-diagrams.tex) with the rebranded dBlue/dFill instance styling. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} because six participants exceed the 13.5cm text block at natural size. Six instances are used (one above the suggested ~5) because the prompt explicitly named all six participants (Operator, Frontend, Gateway, training-match, medical-fitness, DB); messages were kept concise to compensate. Facts grounded in Appendix C (match_events.event_type/minute/player_keycloak_id, injuries.status, match_lineups) and FR-17 (an INJURY event is both a match event and a real injury record that flips the player to injured). The cross-service call training-match -> medical-fitness (POST /injuries) is shown nested inside the same INJURY handling. Endpoints /match-events, /match-lineups (port 8087) and /injuries (port 8086) match the service catalogue in 06-appendices.tex.

label: fig-seq-medical
title: Sequence diagram: injury-to-recovery workflow
caption: Sequence diagram of the injury-to-recovery medical workflow, in which a doctor or physiotherapist advances a player through logged injury, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation and recovery programme via the medical-fitness service, with the staged journey read from the single Injury.status field and only a passing fitness test moving the status to recovered and restoring the player's availability for matches, lineups and training.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdfLaTeX (1 page, no "! " errors; one benign overfull-hbox warning only). Five instances as required: Doctor/Physio (thread), Frontend, Gateway, medical-fitness, DB. The DB only appears explicitly on the initial persist and the final availability-restore call (intermediate POSTs target the medical-fitness instance to keep the diagram readable). The alt fail/pass branches are rendered as self-messages on the medical-fitness lifeline inside an sdblock titled "Fitness test" whose comment carries the "stage read from Injury.status" single-source-of-truth note; the pass branch is the only one that sets status=recovered and triggers availability restoration. Endpoint paths, status values (active/recovering/recovered) and entity names match documentation/chapters/03-methodology.tex and the schema in 06-appendices.tex. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} to fit the A4 text block.

label: fig-seq-messaging
title: Sequence diagram: group messaging over WebSocket with polling fallback
caption: Sequence diagram for group messaging: the front-end opens a WebSocket to \texttt{/ws/chat} on the notification-mail service (outside the gateway) and, when the socket is available, sends a message that the handler persists as a \texttt{Message} keyed by \texttt{group\_id} and broadcasts to connected group members in real time; if the socket is unavailable the client falls back to authenticated HTTP polling of the group's messages.
notes: Compiled clean (pdflatex exit 0, single page, no "!" errors). Five instances per the width constraint: the WebSocketHandler (/ws/chat) instance IS the notification-mail endpoint, so the separate notification-mail lifeline was folded into ":WSHandler /ws/chat" to stay at five columns and fit the 13.5cm text block. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} to scale to text width. Key gotcha fixed during verification: pgf-umlsd's \mess uses its message text as a TikZ node name, so the text must contain no parentheses or commas (these caused "No shape named ''" / "node must have a name" cascades). Message labels were therefore reworded to avoid "(",")","," inside \mess (calls via \begin{call} are unaffected and retain "Message(group_id)"). Facts checked against documentation/chapters/03-methodology.tex (sec:flow-chat) and 06-appendices.tex Appendix C: ws://...:8085/ws/chat outside the gateway, messages table column group_id, polling fallback on GET /messages for the group, real-time broadcast to group members, de-duplication on arrival.

label: fig-seq-ingest
title: Sequence diagram: scheduled external fixture ingestion
caption: Sequence diagram of scheduled external fixture ingestion: the training-match service pulls competition-scoped matches and standings from football-data.org, filters and de-duplicates fixtures before persisting them, reads standings through without storing, and lets the front-end consume the data from the platform's own model.
notes: Compiles cleanly to a single A4 page; the log has no lines starting with "! ", no fatal/emergency errors, and zero over/underfull warnings ("Output written ... (1 page, 16047 bytes)"). pdflatex returns shell exit code 1 (a known benign MiKTeX/pgf-umlsd quirk) but produces a correct PDF. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} because five instances make the diagram wider than the 13.5 cm text block. The external football-data.org instance is reached only by the back-end (training-match service); the Frontend reads exclusively from the platform's /matches model, faithfully reflecting the single-back-end-consumer property. The standings read-through is shown as a self-message on the service to convey "not persisted" without an extra DB write.

label: fig-seq-notify
title: Sequence diagram: event-driven notification via Kafka
caption: Sequence diagram of event-driven notification delivery: the training-match service publishes a domain event to Kafka and returns immediately, while the notification-mail service asynchronously consumes the event, persists a notification, and later surfaces it to the recipient's top-bar bell.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdflatex (1 page, no "! " error lines; exit code 1 is only the benign MiKTeX-update nag). Wrapped in \resizebox to the full \textwidth since five pgf-umlsd instances are wide. Facts taken from documentation/chapters/03-methodology.tex (subsection "Event-Driven Notification Creation via Kafka") and 06-appendices.tex (Appendix C: mscms_notification.notifications table; notification-mail on port 8085; endpoint GET /notifications/recipient/{keycloakId}). Used the concrete event name MatchResultAvailable and the producing service training-match as representative examples; the asynchronous decoupling is shown by the synchronous publish/ack call returning to the producer before Kafka delivers the event to the consumer via an async \mess message.

label: fig-seq-password
title: Sequence diagram: password change with current-password verification
caption: Sequence diagram of the password-change flow, in which the user-management service first verifies the current password via an OAuth~2.0 password-grant exchange against Keycloak and only on success sets the new password through the Keycloak Admin API.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdfLaTeX (exit 0, single page, no "! " or Package/LaTeX errors) via the standalone test documentation/_probe/wf_seq-password.tex, which mirrors probe2.tex's preamble. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} so the 5-instance diagram fits the ~13.5 cm A4 text block. Branch responses use \mess (dashed-return arrows come from the enclosing call return labels); message text deliberately omits quote characters because pgf-umlsd's \mess builds TikZ node names from the message string and quotes/punctuation break node naming. Names and ordering verified against KeycloakAdminImpl.java (verifyPassword does a password-grant on the mscms-frontend client, returning false on 401/invalid_grant; updateUserPassword PUTs to the Admin API /reset-password endpoint) and chapters/03-methodology.tex (subsection "Real-Time Channel and Password Verification", FR-26, PUT /users/{id}/password).

label: fig-state-match
title: State machine: live-match phase progression
caption: State machine for live-match phase progression, where a scheduled match advances through the regulation halves to full time and, for an unresolved knockout tie only, continues into extra time and a penalty shoot-out before finishing.
notes: Compiled cleanly with pdfLaTeX (1 page, no "! " errors). Uses only preamble-diagrams.tex styles (st, initial, accepting, flow, lbl) plus the standard \resizebox. The only log warning is a benign Overfull \hbox of 17.6pt from the resizebox content being scaled to text width. Faithful to chapters/03-methodology.tex Sec 4.6: Scheduled->FirstHalf->HalfTime->SecondHalf->FullTime; the ExtraTime->Penalties->Finished branch is gated by the "knockout & level" condition, while league/friendly (or a level league match) goes from FullTime straight to Finished. State names abbreviated with hyphenation (Sched-uled, Fin-ished, Penal-ties) only to fit the circular st nodes; underlying entity is MatchStatus.

label: fig-state-injury
title: State machine: injury lifecycle and recovery journey
caption: State machine for the injury lifecycle and recovery journey: the Injury.status field drives Active to Recovering to Recovered, with the staged journey (Diagnosis, Treatment, Rehabilitation, Recovery Program, Fitness Test) walked along the transitions, a failed fitness test looping back and a passed test restoring the player to Available.
notes: Verified: standalone wf_state-injury.tex compiled clean with pdflatex (exit 0, no "! " errors, no undefined refs), producing a single A4 page. Faithful to chapters 03 (Injury-to-Recovery workflow, lines 1008-1033) and 06 (mscms_medical schema): Injury.status active->recovering->recovered drives the journey; treatment start flips status to recovering; a passing fitness test sets recovered and restores player Available; a failed test loops back. Journey stages (Diagnosis, Treatment, Rehabilitation, RecoveryProgram, FitnessTest) are rendered as intermediate st states. Laid out across two rows and wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{} to fit the ~13.5cm text block; the failed-test self-loop is drawn on the FitnessTest node (loop below). Uses only st/initial/accepting + lbl and the dLine palette from preamble-diagrams.tex; no extra packages.

label: fig-state-competition
title: State machine: competition lifecycle
caption: State machine for the competition lifecycle: a competition moves from Draft through an editable Ongoing phase to a read-only Completed state once every fixture is played, with the Champions League specialisation in which the knockout bracket stays locked until the league phase is complete.
notes: Compiled cleanly (exit 0, single page, no "! " errors in the log) on the first attempt using documentation/_probe/wf_state-competition.tex with the probe2.tex wrapper. Uses only preamble-diagrams.tex macros (st/initial/accepting state style, flow/flowd/lbl, blue palette). States and transition labels are faithful to FR-12/FR-13 (03-methodology.tex lines 204-206, 231-243; 06-appendices.tex lines 56-57): Draft -> publish -> Ongoing (editable, with a record-result self-loop) -> all fixtures played -> Completed (accepting, read-only badge). The Champions League specialisation is drawn as a dashed link from Ongoing to a League Phase / Knockout (locked) pair, where the knockout unlocks only when the league phase is complete and both rows converge on the same accepting Completed state. Wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} so the two-row automaton fits the ~13.5cm A4 text block.
